title: The Wrong Girls review: Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat shine in stoner buddy comedy
body: Following in the footsteps of Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar and Romy and Michele's High School Reunion, writer/director Dylan Meyer's The Wrong Girls is a sublimely stupid buddy comedy. And thank the movie gods! When it comes to male-fronted buddy comedies, there's no shortage of cinema celebrating loyalty alongside the giddy pleasure of acting really, truly idiotic with your friends. Beyond movies like the Cornetto Trilogy, practically every Kevin Smith movie, or any Will Ferrell comedy, there are also several franchises in this vein, sparked by Dumb and Dumber , Bill Ted ' s Excellent Adventure , and Wayne's World. Female-fronted buddy comedies are fewer and farther between in general, and even more so when it comes to movies that allow the actresses at their center to truly embrace their inner bozo. Sure, in Clueless and Bridesmaids, the heroines make silly mistakes. But they're ultimately relatable and even enviable figures, thanks to their coveted wardrobes, flawless beauty, and dream-guy-secured happy endings. Cheers then to Meyer, who, for her directorial debut, looked at celebrated actresses Alia Shawkat and Kristen Stewart (Meyer's real-life wife), and saw what terrific dum-dums they could be. The Wrong Girls embraces dirtbag girlhood. Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat co-star in "The Wrong Girls." Credit: NEON Stewart and Shawkat star as Frankie and Molly, two best friends who share a home, two cats, a bong, and an utter lack of ambition. title: Booksellers suspect AI firms are buying and then destroying rare books
author: Ashley Belanger
body: If you can truly appreciate an old book—and maybe even marvel at how its fragile, yellowing pages contain some of the earliest ways that people tried to make sense of the world around them—then headlines about tech companies destroying books to train AI likely torture a tender part of your soul. It’s indeed depressing to imagine piles of book spines waiting to be fed into wood chippers while torn-out pages are cropped, scanned, and trashed. But that’s the cheapest and easiest way to scan books as fast as possible, and AI companies are in a race to advance their models by training on the kind of engaging, high-quality, long-form texts that can only be found in books. So book lovers fear it’s likely that the practice is happening on a grander scale than is currently being reported and that some physical copies of books will be lost forever. What makes this destruction extra painful, though, is that it doesn’t have to be this way. Read full article Comments

title: New space object masquerades as a star the size of our solar system
body: Astronomers have found the earliest example of a black hole rapidly bulking up in the universe and it may finally resolve a long‑running cosmic dilemma. The object appears just 660 million years after the Big Bang . Using NASA 's James Webb Space Telescope , researchers found that almost all of its light comes from a central black hole wrapped in a tight shell of stormy hydrogen gas, rather than from stars in a surrounding galaxy. SEE ALSO: Solar Eclipse 2026 livestreams: How to watch safely today without glasses That alone is striking. But what really matters is the clarity of the signal. After using computers to simulate different possibilities, the team was able to rule out stars and dust as the main sources of its incredible light. That makes this object, dubbed MoM-BH*‑1, the strongest evidence yet of a newly proposed type of space object a so-called black hole star giving scientists a firm blueprint for a whole population of puzzling objects Webb has spotted near the beginning of time. "You have something that looks a bit like a star but is 100 billion times brighter," said Rohan Naidu, lead author of the study and an MIT fellow at the time, in a statement. "That means you can't be powering this by nuclear fusion, which is the energy source that sits at the heart of all the stars we have." The object is mind‑boggling: a black hole that is about 100,000 times more massive than the sun , sitting at the center of an enormous ball of gas. Through Webb's eye, it looks like a star the size of our entire solar system. To put it bluntly: "It's huge," said Na

title: The End of Oak Street review: Imagine Jurassic Park but bleak and stupid
body: What if Steven Spielberg were a misanthrope? On its surface, The End of Oak Street plays like a pastiche of Spielberg work, cherry-picking elements from Jaws and Jurassic Park, including signature moments of sound design and score. Yet the question at its core is not really about whether its American nuclear family will survive. (It's a Hollywood summer movie, after all.) It's what happens when the Amblin aesthetic is used as a husk to express a deep disdain for humankind. Warner Bros. gave writer-director David Robert Mitchell (It Follows) a blockbuster budget that enabled top-notch visual effects and A-list stars like Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor. And in return, he gave the studio a survival action movie bursting with ferocious feathered dinosaurs, but also oozing with existential dread and a slyly regressive politics. On its surface, The End of Oak Street looks like summer fun. But it is, in fact, as bleak and infuriating as the recent and alarmingly similar Netflix release The Last House. The End of Oak Street is a gory and mean sci-fi adventure. title: Meet the Pixel Tag, Googles answer to the Apple AirTag
body: Google 's version of the AirTag is coming: The Google Pixel Tag. The Google Pixel Tag uses Google's Find Hub network to help you find your belongings, like your wallet or suitcase. It can be used with Android devices running Android 9 or newer; connect it to your device, name it, and even share it with up to 10 people. SEE ALSO: How to watch Made By Google 2026 You can see your tagged items on the map within the Find Hub app. If you lose something, you can ring it if it's within Bluetooth range, and it'll play a sound through its built-in speaker. Apparently, it'll have precise location data thanks to Ultra-Wideband with Bluetooth Channel Sounding, so you can recover your item even if it's in a nook or cranny. Credit: Ren Ramos / Mashable And if you leave your keys or wallet (or pet?) behind, or are about to, you'll get an alert. You'll also get an alert if an unknown tag is with you. Should your tagged item be out of range, Find Hub will tap into a network of over one billion Android devices to find it, according to Google's press release. Credit: Ren Ramos / Mashable The Google Pixel Tag is made of stainless steel and has a battery life of up to one year (which is similar to the AirTag ). At under two inches long, 0.2 inches thick, and weighing 0.4 ounces, it won't add bulk to your valuables. It retails for $29 for one or $99 for a 4-pack. It releases on Nov. 11.

title: Researchers found a way to hijack devices through Zoom screen sharing
author: Lily Hay Newman, wired.com
body: As AI models gain advanced capabilities to find vulnerabilities in software, develop ways to exploit them , and even carry out autonomous hacking sprees , researchers offered a sobering new example on Tuesday, disclosing vulnerabilities in the video conferencing platform Zoom that could have been exploited to take over targets’ devices. Anyone on a call that involved screen sharing, whether participants or the host, would have been vulnerable to a silent attack that could be carried out with no indication and no interaction from the victim. Researchers from the digital defense firm A Security say the bug was discovered in early June using publicly available AI models, and that it took fewer than 20 prompts to uncover the vulnerabilities and create a working attack. Zoom issued a security advisory on Tuesday, including details about fixes the company has already begun rolling out to address the flaws, which affected devices running all operating systems that Zoom supports—Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. “What is interesting for us and what we believe is dangerous is the democratization of these capabilities—the barrier to entry is dropping rapidly,” A Security cofounder Omer Gull told WIRED ahead of the disclosure. “Before it would have taken a team of five people maybe six months with a lot of refining and iteration to find this. Now people can reach the same results with under 20 prompts. And Zoom is an important type of target because people assume trust when using it. They don’t see it as a threat.” Read full article Comments

title: Formula E finds a new home on Disney+, ESPN+
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Formula E is set to make a big change in terms of visibility when season 12 gets underway this December. It has signed a new multiyear deal to broadcast the sport on Disney+ and ESPN+ in 144 countries, with live coverage of each entire ePrix, from practice through qualifying to the race. The new media deal means that here in the US, Formula E will be shown on ESPN+ from next season; since 2023, the sport has been shown live on Roku. "This is a landmark moment for Formula E and reflects the incredible momentum behind our Championship," said Formula E's CEO Jeff Dodds. "Disney’s unrivaled global reach and storytelling will introduce Formula E to millions of new fans while bringing them closer than ever to the drama, innovation, and excitement of electric racing. As we enter the GEN4 era, this provides an exceptional platform to accelerate our global growth and continue building one of the world’s most exciting sports properties." Actually, the new deal will mean fewer eyeballs on the sport, at least here in the US. More than 100 million US households subscribe to Roku (as of April this year), whereas ESPN+ has been losing subscribers since peaking at the end of 2023 and is now down to roughly 24 million households in the US. title: Did poop enable the evolution of complex animals?
author: Kiona N. Smith
body: The Cambrian explosion may have been fueled by poop. The first animals on Earth emerged about 600 million years ago, and 60 million years later, those simple early animals evolved into wildly different directions, branching out into a diverse menagerie of complicated new forms and conquering new ecological niches. Known as the Cambrian Explosion, this flurry of rapid evolution produced most of the animal phyla and ecosystems we see around us today. And it may have taken off because some of those early animals evolved a bizarre new ability: pooping. According to a recent study, the first poo pellets helped spread nutrients to deeper parts of the ocean, fueling the evolution of bigger animals in more diverse ecosystems. title: This map shows how many Flock cameras are in your neighborhood
body: Flock cameras are swiftly becoming the bane of citizens' existence , with the U.S.-wide network of automated license plate readers (ALPRs) increasingly coming under public scrutiny . Now, there's an app that can show you how many devices owned by surveillance company Flock Safety are in your neighbourhood. Reported by the New York Times , DeFlock Maps is a crowdsourced app aiming for "surveillance transparency " that pinpoints ALPRs including Flocks on a map. SEE ALSO: What are Flock cameras and why are they so controversial? The map uses crowdsourced data from contributors to DeFlock and is powered by open-source project OpenStreetMap . According to the app's website, "Camera locations come from volunteers and the OpenStreetMap community, not a private company or government agency." Devices pinned include not just Flock cameras but those of Motorola Solutions, Genetec, and other unnamed tech companies. However, Flock cameras make up over 80 percent of the devices mapped. "Mass surveillance infrastructure is expanding rapidly in our communities, often without public awareness or consent," DeFlock's user guide reads . "DeFlock makes surveillance infrastructure visible. By documenting these devices and uploading the data to OpenStreetMap, we create a transparent, searchable record of the surveillance apparatus in our communities. Knowledge is power, and transparency is the first step toward accountability." Hellcat hit me with such vexation again and again, as rave reviews rolled in from Fantasia International Film Festival, FrightFest, and Beyond Fest. Over and over, critics danced around the secret at the heart of the film, but none would reveal it. Which was infuriating, as I yearned to know. Spoilers be damned! So, please forgive me as I, too, avoid the major spoiler. But yeah, there'll be some hints along the way that true horror hounds can discern. Hellcat begins as an abduction thriller. Dakota Gorman stars in "Hellcat," a Shudder release. Credit: Shudder Written and directed by Brock Bodell, Hellcat opens with a scene that feels like something out of the true crime series Your Worst Nightmare . A young woman wakes up in the back of a camper trailer. She doesn't know where she is or how she got there, but she can tell this camper is moving. Where? Why? And who put her here? Dakota Gorman stars as this woman, Lena, whose survival instincts kick in quickly and ferociously. Wordlessly, she makes her way up and down the camper, trying to assess how to get out and, failing that, what the hell is going on. Before long, she hears a voice. On Aug. 12, the moon will sweep its shadow across the top of the world, briefly turning day into twilight along a narrow path through Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, northern Spain, and a sliver of Portugal. That's the path of totality where the sun is completely blocked and it's the first time in 27 years that mainland Europe has gotten a full, real-deal solar eclipse. But people in the United States won't be in that bullseye. Instead, a part of the country will see a partial solar eclipse, where the moon nips the sun but never covers it completely. The sky won't go dark, the stars won't pop out, and you won't get the full moody effect . body: Welcome to your guide to Pips, the latest game in the New York Times catalogue. Released in August 2025, Pips puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit. Currently, if you're stuck, the game only offers to reveal the entire puzzle, forcing you to move on to the next difficulty level and start over. However, we have you covered! Below are piecemeal answers that will serve as hints so that you can find your way through each difficulty level. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. SEE ALSO: Wordle today: Answer, hints for August 12, 2026 The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible and common for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space. Here are common examples you'll run into across the difficulty levels: Number : All the pips in this space must add up to the number. Equal : Every domino half in this space must be the same number of pips. Not Equal : Every domino half in this space must have a completely different number of pips. Less than : Every domino

title: Chrome adopts what may be the best protection yet against account takeovers
author: Dan Goodin
body: Google’s Chrome browser has added a new feature that could go a long way in preventing a form of account takeover that’s grown increasingly common as users adopt two-factor authentication, passkeys, and similar protections. The new Chrome protection is known as device-bound session credentials (DBSCs). The measure stores a unique encryption key in a silicon-resident fortress that’s built into the device running the browser. On Windows machines, this fortress is called a TPM, short for Trusted Platform Module. On macOS and iOS, it’s known as a secure enclave. Other platforms have differing names. Recently released versions of Chrome for Windows and macOS generate a key that’s stored in this fortress. An antidote to session cookie theft DBSCs protect against the theft of session cookies, the unique strings of characters that websites store on browsers. Session cookies greatly speed up browsing on sensitive sites that require user authentication. Instead of requiring the exchange of credentials each time a user opens a new site page, the server sets a session cookie that effectively proves the user has already successfully logged in. title: Used EV buying guide: The $30,000 edition
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: A strange thing is happening in the used EV market. Supply is up thanks to an ever-increasing stream of ex-lease cars reaching the market, and yet prices have been going up as well. As a result of America's latest war in the Middle East, used EVs have appreciated by just over 5 percent since February. Despite the stronger pricing, used EV sales have been strong this year—up 25 percent year over year by May, although a weaker June has brought overall sales up just over 20 percent year over year, according to the analysts at Cox Automotive. Used EVs also hang around on dealer lots a lot less than new ones—the same analysts at Cox found just 38 days' supply of used EVs in June, but 81 days for new EVs. And much of the demand is at the cheaper end of the spectrum, say the analysts at Recurrent . In previous installments of our used EV buyers' guide, we've already looked at the most affordable used EVs, ending last time at $25,000 —EVs that may now qualify for a $1,750 rebate if you're in California. Today we're looking at used EVs that cost between $25,000 and $30,000, and according to Autotrader's search, there are more than 9,000 used EVs for sale in that price range. Broadly, you can split the results into three buckets: Cars where you'll find plenty to choose from; ones where there might be a couple of hundred for sale nationwide; and then the oddities where there might just be a handful to pick from. title: Spotify will now tell you when an artist isn’t real
body: That new singer in your Spotify playlist may have a name, a face, and a carefully written bio. Soon, Spotify may also tell you the person they describe doesn t exist. Beginning in mid-September, the streaming platform will place an "AI Persona" badge on profiles built around AI-generated identities. Music from those profiles will also be excluded from Spotify s editorial playlists and algorithmic recommendations by default, the company announced Aug. 11. Spotify will stop introducing listeners to AI Personas by default. Their songs should no longer pop up in Discover Weekly, Release Radar, or another personalized playlist unless you have already shown interest in the artist. You can still search for, play, and follow them, and following one may tell Spotify that you re open to hearing more. Put simply, the company doesn t want an AI Persona to be something you discover by accident. Credit: Spotify That is also the frustration Spotify says it has heard from listeners, who "don t like seeing an artist profile that seems human, only to find out that the persona is AI-generated," according to the announcement. The data suggest plenty of listeners share that concern. As Mashable reported in 2025 , 97 percent of respondents could not distinguish a fully AI-generated song from one made by humans. Still, 80 percent wanted AI music clearly labeled, and 72 percent wanted to know if a streaming service was recommending it. title: Less than 2.5% of Taylor Farms' recalled lettuce went to Taco Bells
author: Beth Mole
body: Though shredded iceberg lettuce at Taco Bell restaurants has been a prime suspect in an explosive outbreak of the diarrheal parasite Cyclospora , a new report from the Food and Drug Administration finally reveals where all the contaminated lettuce was sold—and only a tiny sliver of it went to Taco Bell locations. The feces-tainted lettuce was sourced from Mexico and sold by Taylor Farms, a mammoth produce provider based in California. Taylor Farms has drawn scrutiny for its ties to the Trump administration and reluctance to provide information amid the outbreak, which has now sickened over 23,000 people across 47 states, killing two and sending over 500 others to the hospital. Taylor Farms reportedly attempted to delay issuing a recall amid the illnesses and, since then, has refused to clearly report how much tainted lettuce it recalled and where all of it had been shipped. The FDA's Enforcement Report finally provides some answers: Taylor Farms recalled a total of 236,192 cases of lettuce due to potential Cyclospora contamination. Of those, only 5,900—just shy of 2.5 percent—were sold to Yum, the parent company of Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and KFC. title: Tracking extreme heat by the hour makes climate change seem even worse
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: Global warming is leading to more extremely hot weather. There is perhaps no more obvious consequence of climate change. But changing how we analyze this problem can still help scientists think about it in a different way that may yield surprises. Generally, studies on heat extremes work with some combination of daily minimum, maximum, and mean temperatures. Sometimes they focus on multi-day heatwaves using those metrics, since the discomfort and health impacts increase for longer events. There are different thresholds you can use to define extreme heat in these analyses, either based on past statistics or on the human body’s physiological limits. A new study led by Weilin Liao and Xuanzong Zhang at Sun Yat-sen University tried breaking down heat extremes to the hourly level instead, which reveals some interesting nuances. title: A Google insider spills the tea on how the company forsook its founding ideals
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: In 2018, 20,000 Google employees worldwide made headlines when they staged a walkout to protest how the company had handled sexual misconduct allegations against key corporate executives, among other grievances. One of the organizers was Claire Stapleton , a communications specialist whose distinctive voice and ability to channel the corporate ethos had once earned her the internal moniker "Bard of Google." Six months later, a disillusioned Stapleton resigned, claiming she had been demoted during the most recent restructuring as retaliation for helping to spearhead the walkout. The story of how she went from enthusiastic cheerleader to proactive dissident, and the many lessons she learned along the way, are featured in her new book, Don't Be Evil: Bad Bosses, Fake Promises, and My Escape from Big Tech—A Biting Memoir of Twelve Years Inside Google . Stapleton didn't set out to be a rabble-rouser. When she joined Google out of college in 2007, it was like "getting the golden ticket in Willy Wonka ," she told Ars. Awareness of her good fortune offset any initial uneasiness or skepticism, although Stapleton was sufficiently independent-minded not to move into what was then Google's new corporate housing development in Mountain View, California. Stapleton was very good at her job, and she quickly moved up the ranks, playing a key role in shaping the company's public image. Read full article Comments

title: Trump to give Republicans a 3-1 FCC majority, isn't filling empty Democratic seat
author: Jon Brodkin
body: The Federal Communications Commission has been shorthanded throughout President Trump's second term, but it's about to get a new commissioner. Unsurprisingly, Trump is breaking a historical norm with a nomination that would give Republicans a 3-1 advantage on the FCC. Historically, the president and Senate worked together to ensure that the president's party maintained only a one-vote majority. Normally, the president's party has three FCC members while the minority party has two. Instead of the typical 3-2 split, the FCC has operated with a 2-1 Republican majority during Trump's second term. On Friday, Trump nominated Republican Danielle Thumann Severs to take one of the empty spots. Thumann Severs, a lawyer, has been working as FCC Chairman Brendan Carr's senior counsel. She must be confirmed by the Republican-controlled Senate before being sworn in as a commissioner. Read full article Comments

title: Gentle Monster trailer sees Léa Seydoux facing dark home truths
body: Something's very off in the trailer for Gentle Monster , with L a Seydoux starring as a woman facing dark truths in her own home. And though the film's absolutely not about the Korean eyewear brand , the director was inspired by the company's name . Written and directed by Marie Kreutzer, the film follows concert pianist Lucy (Seydoux) whose idyllic home life with her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) and son is shattered when the police show up with a search warrant, accusing Phillip of a heinous crime. Forced to reckon with the accusations against the person she loves, Lucy has more than one lie to untangle, and her son to protect. It's a complicated film, thematically, for Kreutzer, whose 2022 film Corsage starred actor Florian Teichtmeister, who was charged for similar crimes. The director told The Hollywood Reporter in May 2026, "In the middle of that whole scandal and shit storm, I thought maybe I cannot make Gentle Monster anymore, because everyone will always make that connection. It didn t take me very long until to realize that I might have to make it even more." From the trailer, we get a glimpse of director of photography Judith Kaufmann's cinematography, music by Camille, and a powerful performance from Seydoux, who stars alongside Jella Haase and Catherine Deneuve. Gentle Monster will premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) in September, before its release in select cinemas Oct. 30. The film will then be streaming on Netflix from Nov. 18. title: Claude to start watermarking AI-generated content
body: Anthropic's Claude will start watermarking AI-generated content in compliance with EU rules, the company announced on Tuesday. In a Claude support document, Anthropic wrote that it has signed the EU AI Act's Article 50(2) Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content , and explains how it plans to put those rules into practice. SEE ALSO: Claude Code s auto mode will be on by default, Anthropic confirms Models launched in the EU on or after Aug. 2, 2026, wrote Anthropic, will support watermarking at launch. This includes output from all models including Claude Platform (API), Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and Claude Tag. Generated text will have embedded watermarks, while generated files will include "digitally signed provenance metadata where supported." Notably, it won't apply only to Europe; instead, the watermarks will appear wherever Claude is offered, worldwide, though Anthropic warns that some platforms or features may not support certain watermarking types. Featured Video For You Is ChatGPT Changing the Way We Write? The watermarks won't be visible if you don't know what you're looking for. For text files, the watermark will be "part of the text" and it will "travel with the text when it's copied and pasted elsewhere," but Anthropic doesn't really go into the technicalities of how this will work. title: New surveillance tech links your phone to your license plate
author: Nicole M. Bennett, The Conversation
body: Imagine that you share a ride to work with the same colleague most mornings. As it passes by a license plate reader, the camera records the car, which can be linked through vehicle records to its registered owner. Beside it, another sensor detects signals broadcast by devices traveling nearby, such as your phone and your colleague’s smartwatch. After enough trips, software may treat some of those devices as a recurring electronic signature associated with the vehicle. Weeks later, one of the same device signals appears alongside a different car connected to an investigation. The signal itself may not contain its owner’s name, but its previous association with a known vehicle gives investigators another clue they can use to work out who was carrying the device. SignalTrace , a system marketed by the security company Leonardo , is designed to work alongside automatic license plate readers. The company says it can recognize groups of consumer devices that regularly move together, then associate them with license plate records and time-stamped locations. The pattern can then be searched even when a police investigator does not know the plate number. Read full article Comments

title: New Pass-ta-key attack reveals all the things we didn't know about passkeys
author: Dan Goodin
body: Last week a researcher outlined what he said was a “novel attack surface” in passkeys, the new authentication paradigm that offers a more secure alternative over password-based methods. In fact, the attacks demonstrated in the post are neither novel nor unique to passkeys. This distinction is important because the research has generated confusion among end users and security professionals as they assess whether this new mechanism is truly safe to use. The attack is called Pass-ta-key—a blending of the word passkey with the phrase “pass the key” and a nod to a plate of pasta. Arie Olshtein, a researcher at security firm Palo Alto Networks, described in a post last week how Pass-ta-key could obtain all passkeys stored in the Google Password Manager app (GPM) for Windows when it’s running on a machine infected with malware. This came as a surprise to many people because they believed passkeys are stored exclusively in the trusted platform manager (TPM), the locked-down enclave in a hardened silicon chip that’s reserved for storing cryptographic keys and other highly sensitive information on Windows machines. If passkeys are stored in the TPM, then how was Pass-ta-key able to extract the entire set of passkeys stored by the app, they wanted to know. Read full article Comments

body: Tesla 's Cybercabs now come with built-in Starlink connectivity. On Monday, the company's Robotaxi account on X shared photos of the first Cybercab with an integrated Starlink antenna. Check it out up close in the photo below. It fits nicely. But is it needed? Credit: Tesla Given that Starlink is best suited for remote areas where there's no 5G connectivity, and Cybercabs will almost certainly first start operating in dense urban areas , why do Tesla's autonomous taxis even need Starlink? Cybercabs have 5G chips built-in, and the Starlink antenna adds additional cost, weight, and complexity which doesn't appear necessary right now. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has the answer, and it's definitely, absolutely, certainly not so that Tesla can foot another bill to Musk-owned SpaceX . In a tweet , he referenced Cloudflare's assessment that "bot traffic will exceed human (internet) traffic by a factor of 1,000 within five years." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. "And the only system that can support the insanely fast bandwidth growth needed by AI is Starlink," wrote Musk in a reply. Ever since SpaceX's monster IPO in June, there's been talk about SpaceX and Tesla merging into one giant corporation that covers transportation, energy, AI, chipmaking, and AI compute, both on Earth and in space. title: Rare Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt variant discovered, to auction this week
body: Almost 100 rare Nintendo cartridges have been discovered in a Wisconsin retro games store, with a handful of them to go up for auction this week. The individually wrapped Super Mario Bros ./ Duck Hunt NES cartridges appear to have come from a previously unknown run of the games, with collectors having been unaware of their existence until now. SEE ALSO: 'The Super Mario Galaxy Movie' review: Death is coming for us all The 97 Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt cartridges belong to Kevin Braun, owner of retro games store OneStopWonders in Waukesha, Wisconsin, and were identified with the help of Nintendo Wire editor Jason Ganos. Nintendo Wire reports that the cartridges were initially in the possession of a precious metal recovery service, which Nintendo appeared to have contracted to break them down. They were left untouched for decades, until Braun purchased the box of games from the owner's grandson. He had been intending to sell the games at OneStopWonders, but forgot them in a storage unit until they came up in conversation with Ganos. "After Kevin finished his story, I immediately could tell that the blood had drained from my face," Ganos wrote, recounting the discovery on Nintendo Wire. Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt aren't rare games in and of themselves. Released in the U.S. alongside the NES' 1985 launch, Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt have left enduring legacies as two of the platform's most popular titles. In 1988, the games were put together in dual cartridges and sold with the NES in an Action Set bundle. However, Braun's cartridges do not appear to be from this run.

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 11
body: We're almost at the end of the Moon's current lunar cycle, with only the tiniest sliver surface still visible. That crescent will to shrink nothing over the next few nights before the Moon reaches its New Moon phase. What is today s Moon phase? As of Tuesday, Aug. 11, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 3% of its surface visible. The Moon is not illuminated enough to be able to spot anything on its surface tonight. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon doesn't look the same from Earth every night. As it travels around our planet, it moves through a lunar cycle that takes roughly 29.5 days to complete, according to NASA . The changing positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon affect how much of the Moon's sunlit side we can see, creating the different phases. Over the course of the cycle, the Moon progresses from a narrow crescent to a half Moon and eventually a Full Moon, before starting the sequence over again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) T

title: Trump signs bonkers order that cuts vaccines, promotes ones that don't exist
author: Beth Mole
body: President Trump signed an executive order Monday that makes sweeping, unilateral changes to federal vaccine recommendations. The order aims to reduce the number of lifesaving vaccines all children are recommended to get—from 18 to 11—while also splitting them up and spacing them out over more time and more medical visits. The vaccine changes are not backed by evidence or spurred by new findings. Rather, they are based on false anti-vaccine fearmongering about harms, including the debunked claim that they cause autism, and misinformation that multiple vaccinations can "overwhelm" children's immune systems. This false claim has also been repeatedly debunked and explained . During a signing event at the White House on Monday afternoon, Trump falsely claimed that pediatricians "have a vaccination that looks like the size of a bottle of soda," that is "poured into a little child's body, and bad things happen in too many cases. This is an explosion; this is an epidemic," Trump said. Read full article Comments

title: Amazon backs power plant that may become top source of US climate pollution
author: Ashley Belanger
body: Amazon’s artificial intelligence ambitions will soon be partly fueled by a natural gas-burning power plant in Texas that “could become the largest single source of climate pollution in the United States,” The New York Times reported . These gas-burning plants are increasingly lumped into data center projects. They produce harmful pollutants, which can accelerate climate change impacts and harm public health—contributing to conditions like asthma, heart disease, lung cancer, and strokes. Some communities are demanding more stringent environmental reviews, but the Trump administration favors fast-tracking that can include skipping the permitting process entirely. Since Elon Musk’s xAI controversially began relying on gas turbines last spring to power its biggest AI data center, Colossus, there has been public backlash to off-the-grid data centers like the one Amazon is building. title: Amazons robotaxi Zoox launches first paid service in U.S.
body: There s a new robotaxi in town Amazon's Zoox . Paid rides on Zoox became available for the first time ever, with service launching in Las Vegas on Monday (Aug. 10). The Sin City service follows Zoox's recent availability as a free option for select San Francisco riders. While Alphabet's autonomous Waymo cars are also available in Vegas , Zoox has some distinct differences, most notably its carriage-style seating made possible by the absence of a steering wheel and gas pedal. Zoox vehicles also lack a formal front or rear, allowing them to drive in either direction seamlessly. Riders adjust temperature and music choices on screens in the cabin. On July 30, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration announced that Zoox could temporarily offer paid service . "This temporary exemption will allow the commercial deployment of up to 2,500 vehicles annually for two years, subject to an enhanced, adaptable oversight structure that can evolve as Zoox s technology advances," according to the agency. Zoox prices will be competitive with other rideshare services, according to the Los Angeles Times , with possible surcharges for trips to airports or special events. The Zoox app shows rides currently available in a wide swath of the Las Vegas Valley, with vehicles operating from 11 a.m. to 1 a.m. On-demand service in Austin, Miami, and San Francisco will be up next. Waymo recently announced its van-style Ojai service is available for free to select riders in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix. title: Supergirls Milly Alcock and Jason Momoa weigh in why nice isnt all that super
body: Supergirl is flying into theaters, and DC fans have plenty of reason to rejoice. The spinoff from 2025's Superman follows Kara (Milly Alcock), Clark Kent's cousin from Krypton, as she pub-crawls across the cosmos. Her plans for devil-may-care merriment are disrupted, however, when she crosses paths with an orphaned girl named Ruthye (Eve Ridley) on a quest for vengeance. Whether Supergirl likes it or not, she can't help but be the hero and the role model Ruthye needs. And along the way, she'll run into fiends and foes, including the outrageous bounty hunter Lobo ( Jason Momoa ). But above all, she offers a lesson that seems to fly in the face of her chipper cousin: Don't be nice. Be kind. When Entertainment Editor Kristy Puchko sat down in virtual interviews with Alcock, Momoa, and Supergirl screenwriter Ana Nogueira, they dug into what exactly that means. What's so bad about being nice? And what distinguishes being kind and being nice? And where does Lobo fit into this? You better believe Momoa and company had thoughts. Supergirl opens in theaters on June 26.

title: 911 calls are getting the AI treatment now
body: New Orleans, home to more than 300,000 residents and an emergency system that handles thousands of calls each day, is turning to AI for help. The city recently confirmed that emergency services, overseen by the Orleans Parish Communication District, are deploying an AI triage tool to screen and sort incoming calls to assist human operators. City representatives explained the technology is intended to reduce the number of repetitive calls and prevent lines from bottlenecking. Basically, if a resident calls in an incident that's already been reported, like a car crash, the AI dispatcher is supposed to handle it. SEE ALSO: AI companies keep destroying old books. Here's why. The tool, referred to as AI Emergency Call Triage, was developed by AI emergency services company Carbyne. It's still undergoing real-world testing by operators, according to reporting by the Shreveport Times, but has been involved in triaging traffic-related emergency calls since at least 2023 . The city also introduced an AI tool for its 311 non-emergency services in April. New Orleans is one of several cities introducing AI into emergency and non-emergency call operations, and Carbyne is already working with public safety agencies across the country. In 2024, the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) published a fact sheet exploring the implementation of AI into emergency service operations, including testimony from early adopters like the Orleans Parish Communication District. title: YouTube just raised the bar for creators to earn ad revenue
body: YouTube built one of the creator economy 's biggest payment systems, but now it is raising the bar for who gets to share in it. Beginning Feb. 1, 2027, new creators will need 8,000 qualified watch hours over the previous year or 20 million qualified Shorts views within 90 days to earn advertising and YouTube Premium revenue, the company announced Aug. 10 . This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Both figures are double YouTube's current requirements of 4,000 watch hours or 10 million Shorts views. The announcement did not mention a change to the existing requirement that creators have at least 1,000 subscribers. The new rules will also affect creators who are already part of the YouTube Partner Program. To earn ad and subscription revenue from Shorts each month, they will need to maintain 10 million qualified views during a rolling 90-day period. Channels that fall below the threshold will remain in the program and can continue making money from long-form videos. Shorts revenue sharing will resume automatically if their views climb back above it. YouTube said creators who already earn "significant revenue" from Shorts are unlikely to be affected, but did not disclose how many channels currently fall short of the requirement. The updates mark the first significant overhaul of the Partner Program since 2018. More than 3 million creators now participate in the program, which distributes revenue from advertising and subscriptions and provides access to fan contributions and shopping tools. title: Taylor Farms recalls jalapeño products for Salmonella amid Cyclospora outbreak
author: Beth Mole
body: Amid a massive Cyclospora outbreak linked to its iceberg lettuce, Taylor Farms is now recalling products containing jalapeños, which were linked last week to a large, multi-state Salmonella outbreak. On Sunday, August 9, Taylor Farms recalled jalapeño-containing products , including diced jalapeños, dips, salsas, pico de gallo, guacamole, and pre-made salads, burritos, and sandwiches. The foods, which include both branded and unbranded products, were sold across 26 states at major retailers, including Hannaford, Kroger, Target, Trader Joe's, Walmart, and Whole Foods. The recalled products contain recalled jalapeños from Coast Citrus Distributors , which was linked last week to a Salmonella outbreak that has infected at least 345 people across 27 states , sending at least 36 people to the hospital. No deaths have been reported. Read full article Comments

title: Claude Code’s auto mode will be on by default, Anthropic confirms
body: Anthropic's AI programming tool just made a somewhat big change. In a blog post , Anthropic announced that "auto mode" will, going forward, be turned on by default in Claude Code for anyone with a Pro, Max, or Team account. The change takes effect on Aug. 14, though you might get a prompt asking if you want to turn on auto mode depending on what settings you've chosen for yourself. SEE ALSO: Shared a Claude conversation? Google may have seen it. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. For the uninitiated (read: me), auto mode in Claude Code stops asking for human prompts at each step of the development process, instead giving the AI agent permission to proceed on its own unless the action it's taking would be destructive or impossible to reverse. That sounds like it'd be difficult to trust as a programmer, but Anthropic claims that in testing, auto mode caught 89 percent of harmful actions, while real humans only caught 13.6 percent. And now, that will be the out-of-the-box experience for Claude Code users. As always, though, you can still turn it off.

No Ordinary Love continued last year with five additional stories published weekly on Substack. They were penned by five new writers, including Hunter Harris, who wrote the audiobook's foreword. SEE ALSO: Hinge founder's AI matchmaker coming later this year The audios are available now on Substack , Spotify , Libro.fm , Apple Audiobooks , Barnes Noble Audiobooks , and the library app Libby . "Hinge continues to find inspiration in the rise of book-focused conversations on social media and how it deeply resonates with Gen Z," the company told The Bookseller. "Romance is the most popular genre read by 18 to 29-year-olds, and audiobooks are growing in popularity with readers, who listen as they go about their daily lives." body: SteamOS is continuing its slow march to fuller support on a wider variety of non-Valve hardware. This weekend's release of the SteamOS 3.8.25 Beta includes "initial gamepad support" for a few recent gaming handhelds and improved support for a few others. Those newly supported handhelds include MSI's Claw 8 EX AI+, the extremely expensive , extremely powerful handheld built around Intel's Arc G3 processor that launched this summer. While SteamOS has long included beta support for "other AMD powered handhelds," Valve has only recently been working on offering compatibility with Intel-based handhelds like the MSI Claw line. title: Spotify is testing a skip button that might let you skip podcast ads
body: Spotify has rolled out a feature that lets some users skip past podcast ads not sold directly by the platform, per an exclusive report from Semafor . In the report, Spotify frames the change as a streamlined version of its existing skip button, but publishers say it could gut their ad revenue. According to Semafor, Podnews called the update a "significant threat" to ad-funded shows, while Crooked Media co-founder Tommy Vietor was more direct, writing on social media that it was "very cool" of Spotify to "try and destroy the podcast industry." SEE ALSO: Spotify hits 300 million Premium subscribers Semafor reported that several major audio networks contacted Spotify directly after the announcement to raise concerns about their monetization. Privately, the company has argued that the feature actually helps publishers by keeping people listening longer overall, citing internal engagement data, while also stressing that the button is still in early testing and could be pulled back. A Spotify spokesperson confirmed to Semafor that the rollout is limited to certain paid subscribers and only appears when the app is open in the foreground, describing it as part of routine product testing aimed at making podcast listening "more intuitive" for Premium users. The move lands as the podcast industry is already contending with a broader shift toward video platforms like YouTube, Semafor noted, and it isn't the first time Spotify has drawn pushback from publishers the company partially reversed a podcast play-count rollout last year after similar complaints.

title: Following Epic loss, Google has started hosting rival app stores in the Play Store
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: A new day has dawned in the Play Store, and it's one that Google tried very hard to avoid. The first third-party app store has arrived in Google Play as a result of the long-running antitrust lawsuit with Epic . Those in the US can now head into Google Play and download Aptoide , a game-focused store that has been available as a sideloaded client since the early days of Android. Forcing Google to distribute third-party app stores in Google Play was one of several remedies imposed by Judge James Donato after Epic emerged victorious in 2023. The remedies also included lowering developer fees, mirroring Google Play apps in other app stores, and allowing developers to use alternative payment systems. But it was the app store stipulation that seemed to irk Google the most. Google almost avoided this outcome when it agreed to a settlement with Epic , which was announced early this year. Under the terms, Google would certify third-party app stores to allow users to install and use them with less friction, but it would not host them in Google Play. However, Google and Epic withdrew the settlement when it appeared the court would not approve it. This Registered App Store program is still slated to launch internationally, but in the US, Google is only doing what it must to comply with the judge's orders. Read full article Comments

title: Metas Muse Glimmer wants to bring AI agents to your laptop
body: Meta thinks the next front in the AI race may be sitting on your desk. On Aug. 10, Meta released Muse Glimmer , a 30-billion-parameter AI model designed to run locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. Its weights are available to download from Hugging Face under a permissive Apache 2.0 license, allowing developers to use, modify, and build products with the model for free. That means Muse Glimmer can operate without sending every request to a distant data center. It can also work without an internet connection, provided the computer running it has enough memory and processing power. For anyone ready to open an app and start chatting, however, there is a catch: Muse Glimmer is a developer release. Meta is supplying the model that can power an AI agent, rather than a consumer product that immediately manages your inbox or reorganizes your desktop. What can Muse Glimmer actually do? Meta built Muse Glimmer for "agentic" work, meaning it can take a goal, divide it into steps, and use connected tools to complete parts of the task. The company imagines local agents that could manage schedules, draft messages, organize files, and write or debug code. The model can process images alongside text, perform multi-step tasks, and attempt recovery when a tool fails. Meta says it was trained on data from more than 100 languages. Fitting those abilities onto one computer required some downsizing. At full precision, Muse Glimmer would need more than 55 GB of memory. title: Dogs can tell if you're scared or sad
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Any dog owner would tell you that their canine companions are attuned to their humans' emotional state and respond accordingly. Scientists have performed fMRI scans on dogs and identified a specific brain region that processes happy human facial expresses, like a smile, according to a new paper published in the journal iScience. They also found that dogs can tell the difference between negative facial expressions, specifically anger, sadness, and fear. “Humans are really good at picking up small details on the face, and so are dogs,” said co-author Raúl Hernández-Pérez of the University of Vienna. “This makes dogs very interesting. By studying their brains, we can understand what adaptations have developed to support their remarkable social and emotional understanding of humans.” Prior behavioral studies have shown that dogs are sensitive to emotion in human faces. Dogs will, for example, choose a box their human has identified with a happy expression over one the human treats with fear or disgust. Past fMRI studies found that an area in the canine left temporal cortex showed a stronger response to human faces compared to dog faces, as well as a greater response in the caudate, hippocampus, and amygdala to human faces showing emotion versus neutral faces. body: When station wagons headed for the same retirement home as the vinyl roof and the opera window, Subaru looked at its sensible Legacy wagon and had a different idea. Raise it a few inches, wrap the lower body in plastic cladding, name it for the Australian bush, and suburban families would drive to soccer practice while imagining themselves fording streams and climbing sand dunes. In giving birth to the Legacy Outback in 1995, Subaru more or less created the template for the modern, adventure-minded, off-road-themed crossover. By the 2000 model year, the Outback had graduated from trim level to standalone model, and it has been paying the bulk of Subaru's bills ever since. Today, the 2026 Outback marks a new era in the model's history. The wagon silhouette that defined six generations has given way to a sharpened two-box shape that's much more at home parked next to an upright Forester or Ascent. title: A researcher bought noreply.net. Companies started sending him secrets.
author: Matt Burgess, wired.com
body: Cory Solovewicz receives more unwanted emails than you. Seriously—it’s a lot more. Since December 2024, one of the domains at which the security researcher receives email has registered 401,796 messages—by his calculations that’s an average of 699.99 pings per day. This deluge isn’t the regular flood of spam, newsletters, and unwanted deals that fill many people’s inboxes. Instead, companies and other organizations are inadvertently sending Solovewicz other people’s private information and company secrets. Over the last few years, he’s received injury reports from a city government, confirmation of people’s pizza orders, and account setup emails from a school platform. “I get service orders for people that need repairs. I get lots of test platform credentials,” says Solovewicz , a security researcher and consultant. Solovewicz is receiving the avalanche of messages as he’s the owner of the domains noreply.us and noreply.net , which he purchased in 2020 and 2024, respectively. After originally planning to use the noreply.us domain as a catch-all email—which receives mail sent to any @ address on that domain—to filter messages and enhance his privacy, the researcher quickly noticed that other systems were sending mail to @ noreply.us addresses. “I created an accidental honeypot,” Solovewicz tells WIRED. “I had no idea it was going to turn into this.” Read full article Comments

The focus on research is still there, but she’s sold off Bose Professional , acquired the high-end audio brands McIntosh Labs and Sonus faber , and, perhaps most importantly, started licensing all that core Bose technology to other companies. title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 survives the ultimate stress test
body: Foldable phones have been around for a while, but I still regularly get people asking me whether they're going to break in half. On Sunday, YouTuber JerryRigEverything tried to do just that to Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 ...and couldn't. SEE ALSO: Review: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 makes phones interesting again JerryRigEverything put Samsung's foldable through his typically rough set of tests to see how it'll hold up. This included scratching the display with a utility knife and burning it with a lighter. The damage was there, of course, but it wasn't fatal. Then, JerryRigEverything tried the ultimate test by bending the phone in the direction opposite of its folding mechanism. Again, there was significant damage to the phone's hinge, and this is something that you should never do to your phone. At the end of it, however, the phone was still alive and kicking, and there was barely any damage to its display. Being limited to one device only, the test obviously isn't perfect, but it's a testament to how far Samsung has progressed in building its foldable phones to last. As a reminder, check out what the same YouTuber's tests did to the original Samsung Galaxy Fold a few years back .

To get the reboot right, Kris travels to the abandoned summer camp where the first movie was shot so she can meet Presley, who's now an eccentric recluse. The company, which created the world's first modular exoskeleton, has launched its H Series, now available for purchase: the H Pro and the H Ultra . Both are built around hip-level assistance that syncs with your natural gait rather than overriding it, stepping in to help during key phases of a stride, like lifting your leg or pushing off the ground. The idea is to cut down on effort, not replace how you move. The H Pro is the lighter, more everyday option, built for walking, fitness, and lighter outdoor activity, with up to 25 kilometers of assisted range. Ascentiz says it delivers up to 1,000W of peak boost, making strides feel about 40% lighter, and it weighs just 5.5 pounds. The H Ultra is the heavier-duty version, with a carbon-fiber and titanium-alloy frame, a dual-battery setup that extends range to 50 kilometers, and higher power output for longer trips. title: Peer review is overwhelmed—can it survive in the AI era?
author: Saima Sidik
body: Jason Semprini was excited about his research on policies mandating that elementary school students receive the human papillomavirus vaccine. HPV causes most cases of cervical cancer, but counterintuitively, Semprini found that mandates don’t do that much to reduce the overall rate of cervical cancer in a population. That’s odd, but it's also not completely surprising—we know that mandating a vaccine can motivate some people to find ways to avoid it. Semprini wrote up the study and submitted the manuscript to a journal, where it was sent out for peer review, a long-standing process through which other researchers in the field assess the validity of research and make a recommendation on whether or not it should be published. This is usually done anonymously and on a volunteer basis. In this case, the reviewer did not share Semprini’s excitement. That may have stemmed from a misunderstanding of the study’s central message: The reviewer mistakenly thought Semprini was questioning whether the HPV vaccine itself prevents cervical cancer rather than studying the effectiveness of a policy meant to increase vaccination rates. “There’s a very big difference there,” said Semprini, who is a health economist at Des Moines University. title: A major Apple Watch redesign may be coming
body: Apple is considering a major overhaul of its Apple Watch, though what exactly that means is still very uncertain. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says that the company's next Apple Watch versions that are coming out this year will only get "modest upgrades," which includes a performance boost, new colors and bands, health and fitness upgrades, and possibly a ceramic case variant, though it's unclear whether that'll happen this or next year. In the future, however, bigger changes are in the works. According to Gurman, Apple is looking into wearables of all sorts, including ones with no displays, and those with different types of screens and various sizes. Yes, that's pretty vague, but when you consider that Apple Watch has pretty much looked the same since day one, it would be a pretty big move by Apple. Apple is also reportedly considering premium models "beyond the Ultra and Herm s variants," as well as cheaper models than the Apple Watch SE. It's early days, and Gurman says the company hasn't settled on a single direction yet, and that the changes will "take time." SEE ALSO: The latest iPhone 18 news, leaks, and rumors: Release date, price increases, and color options Gurman also touched on the iPhone, saying that Apple is already planning a second and a third version of its upcoming foldable iPhone, scheduled to arrive in 2027 and 2028, respectively. title: The solar eclipse is this week — but dont take photos of it with your phone
body: I learned that my iPhone 15 Pro Max and the upcoming 2026 total solar eclipse do not mix. I stumbled upon BGR' s article, which warned skygazers against using their phones to take pictures of the imminent cosmic event. If you're like me, you may be wondering "Why?" After all, who wouldn't want to snap a photo of such an awe-inspiring celestial occurrence? As it turns out, taking a photo of the 2026 solar eclipse could damage your iPhone's camera hardware. SEE ALSO: Solar eclipse 2026 from the US: how to watch from home and online Why you shouldn't take a photo of the 2026 solar eclipse with your phone In the same way that you shouldn't use a telescope or binoculars to gaze at the sun (you could melt your eyeballs off), you shouldn't use your phone's shooter or any other poorly equipped camera to take a photo of the solar eclipse. BGR says that no smartphone is designed to handle the intense solar rays the sun emanates. "Using your camera or phone could cause the heat from the rays to become so concentrated that it could melt the lens inside," the tech outlet warned. Days before the April 8, 2024 eclipse that swept across parts of North America, NASA provided similar advice. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. There is a workaround in that you can purchase filters for your phone and camera . NEEWER 67mm Clip On Filters Kit for Phone Camera Credit: Amazon But the best way to see the eclipse might very well be with your eyes rather than a camera lens. That is, if they are fully protected. title: Hurdle hints and answers for August 10, 2026
body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 10
body: If you thought the Moon looked small last night, it'll be even thinner this evening as it continues to wane ahead of the New Moon in a few night's time. What is today s Moon phase? As of Monday, Aug. 10, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 16% of its surface visible. To see anything on the Moon's surface tonight, you'll need either binoculars or a telescope. With these, you'll be able to see the Grimaldi Basin , a huge ancient crater on the Moon, formed by a massive asteroid collision. Its center was later flooded with dark basalt rock, creating the distinctive shadowy area surrounded by a brighter rim. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance changes throughout the month as it orbits Earth, completing one full lunar cycle approximately every 29.5 days, according to NASA . During that journey, the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon are constantly shifting, altering how much of the Moon's illuminated surface is visible from our perspective. That's why we see the familiar sequence of phases, from a slim crescent to a half Moon, then a Full Moon, before the pattern begins again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.
